actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The project describes itself as a control-system implementation for the Unitree G1 humanoid simulated with the MuJoCo physics engine, covering whole-body control, walking, squatting, arms and fingers
The project advertises full 53-degree-of-freedom whole-body control of the G1
The documented way to run the simulation is `python deploy/deploy_mujoco53.py`
The deployment script imports mujoco and mujoco.viewer
main() requires a positional config_file argument for the deployment config
main loads the MJCF named by the config with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(xml_path), builds MjData, and overwrites model.opt.timestep with config.simulation_dt
main opens a passive MuJoCo viewer over the model and data
The simulation loop advances the model with mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
The config points xml_path at resources/g1/scene53.xml
The config sets simulation_dt to 0.002 s
The scene model is named g1_53dof scene and includes g1_53dof.xml
The scene worldbody contains a plane floor named floor
The scene adds free-floating box1 and box2 bodies to the included robot
The scene adds two drawer slide joints with range -0.8 to 0
The scene adds a free-floating glass_panel body
The included robot model is named g1_53dof and its compiler uses radians with meshes under meshes/
The robot pelvis body sits at 0.80 -1.55 0.763 and carries a free joint named floating_base_joint
The actuator section declares one motor actuator per robot joint (53 motors) and none of them carries a ctrlrange attribute

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in cap.world.reset.v1 but a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults and does not use it, so one control sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  The package's stand-in is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the scene and its include for the free joints, the 53 hinge joints, the 53 motor actuators, their (absent) ctrlranges and the 0.002 s deployed step, then gives each actuated hinge or slide a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds every other joint where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory

the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the scene's boxes, cup, cabinets, glass panel and table geometry, the floor and the robot's collision geoms are not applied

the scene declares no ctrlrange on any of the 53 motors, so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound; the model constrains joint positions and torques, not the motor control value

the world state carries the full 83 qpos and 79 qvel values of the scene (3 scene free bodies, 2 drawer slides, the robot free base and 53 robot hinges); the stand-in holds the three scene free bodies and the two drawer slides fixed, while MuJoCo would simulate them

the upstream deployment script overwrites the model time step with its config value 0.002 s and runs a policy and arm/finger controller in a passive viewer; this package loads the scene directly, serves the step of the model and takes the caller's 53-element control vector
the fake reset restores the parsed model qpos0 and zeros; a real MjData reset also restores the full integration state, which this package did not inspect
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
no physical humanoid is modelled and nothing was validated against Unitree G1 hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
